newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mixed in Tuesday's liquid market, dealers said.

They said the Reserve Bank auctioned Z$400 million worth of treasury bills in the market on Monday at 17.57 percent. The bank was looking to sell Z$450 million worth of the 91-day paper on Tuesday, with Z$600 million maturities anticipated.
Discount houses were selling treasury bills in the market at 17.50 percent, unchanged from Monday, and call money also held steady at 17.50 percent.

Bankers acceptance bills were trading at 17.75 and 17.50 percent (buying and selling) from 18 and 17.75 percent while NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90-days were being bought at 18.65 percent from 18.50 and sold at 18.40 from 18 percent.
Reserve Bank figures indicated a Z$80.6 million surplus for Monday, up from Z$18.3 million the previous day.
